study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities uncover two robust transdiagnostic biotypes

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Identify transdiagnostic subtypes based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities derived via normative modeling, and test their reproducibility, generalizability, and biological underpinnings.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Reproducibility via subsampling and HYDRA with ARI; generalizability to independent SCZ and to unseen MDD by centroid transfer; associations between subtype abnormality patterns and structural covariance neighbors (SC-informed differential pattern); multilinear models linking abnormalities to PET-derived neurotransmitter receptor/transporter maps with dominance analysis; correlations with transcriptional profiles of inflammation-related genes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two robust transdiagnostic subtypes with opposing GMV abnormality patterns were identified, reproducible within discovery data and generalizable to independent SCZ and unseen MDD; subtype 1 abnormalities align more with excitatory receptors, while subtype 2 align more with inhibitory receptors and inflammation-related gene expression.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using ROI-level normative modeling (GPR on age/sex) to derive 246-D z-score maps, k-means (silhouette-selected k=2) revealed two subtypes with contrasting GMV patterns vs HCs. Reproducibility was supported by subsampling (90% resamples, ARI computed over 1000 iterations) and by HYDRA cross-validation (max ARI at k=2). Cluster centroids generalized to COBRE SCZ and predicted subtype labels in DIRECT MDD. SC-informed analyses showed subtype-specific disease epicenters (e.g., hippocampus, ACC, striatum, insula). Multilinear models (FDR<0.001) related subtype patterns to PET-derived receptor/transporter maps, with dominance analysis indicating excitatory receptor predominance in subtype 1 and inhibitory predominance in subtype 2. Subtype 2 abnormalities correlated with transcriptional profiles of inflammation-related genes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: K-means clustering on individualized z-score maps with TIV, age, sex covariates in group comparisons; HYDRA used as a complementary semi-supervised approach for subtype validation; single-site selection (DIRECT site 20) to avoid multi-site effects.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limited range of disorders analyzed; insufficient clinical covariates (e.g., education, alcohol, medication dosage) to assess their effects; comorbidities not modeled.
